design_decisions.decision: The kernel is a normalization + policy layer ON TOP of the three PoC adapters; it does not replace them and does not feed the S0 gate (the gate calls the PoCs directly and compares against the Python Oracle). Nothing in T006 can move the frozen S0 gate hash.
design_decisions.why: The PoCs are the S0-frozen production side; the kernel's job is a single auditable contract (AuditResult) for T009/T013, not a second implementation of host rules.

design_decisions.consequence: The resolver strips PoC SCOPE_LEAK findings and recomputes them via src/policy, so the kernel is the single source of policy truth. Callers must pass the profile policy to the kernel; with no policy argument the kernel emits no policy findings (proven by test on claude/c07).
design_decisions.decision: Policy comparison runs over the EFFECTIVE set = ELIGIBLE instances only. DISCOVERED instances (host found the skill but a flag keeps it unloaded, e.g. OpenMausBot skillsLibrary/claudeUserSkills off) cannot leak and cannot mismatch.
design_decisions.why: A DISCOVERED skill is not loadable, so reporting a leak for it would be a false positive — the failure class SkillScope exists to eliminate. Divergence from the Claude/OpenMausBot PoC inline checks (which count DISCOVERED as effective) is deliberate and documented here; the S0 fixtures do not decide the question (no fixture puts a DISCOVERED instance in a forbidden scope — o09 has no policy at all). Proven by test: o09 + forbiddenScopes [SHARED_LIBRARY] → PoC flags SCOPE_LEAK, kernel reports none, status PASS.

design_decisions.decision: Audit-layer instance identity is the canonical key <sourceRootId>:<relativePath> (the same identity the S0 canonical form uses for finding references).
design_decisions.note: Physical-file identity (one instance per real file) stays with the T005 IdentityRegistry, whose input contract is absolute canonical paths. The kernel deliberately does not fabricate absolute paths to feed the registry: PoC results do not carry them uniformly.
design_decisions.why: Codex native ids are hashes of machine-local absolute paths and OpenMausBot native ids are snapshot-entry ids (<rootId>:<sha256 of canonical path>); both are replaced so kernel output is portable. The kernel builds a native → canonical id map per audit (identity for Claude) and translates finding references through it, throwing on ambiguous or unknown ids — the same guard the S0 canonicaliser applies. This was a real bug found by the tests: the first run failed 3 tests on untranslated OpenMausBot snapshot ids (o06, o07); fixed by the map, not by weakening the check.

design_decisions.decision: DISABLE_MISMATCH is produced only by the kernel (no PoC emits it): an ELIGIBLE instance whose logicalName is in policy.forbiddenNames. Names match exactly, namespace included — forbidden 'deploy' does not match 'acme:deploy'.
design_decisions.why: PROJECT_BOOK §5.2 defines the finding as expected-disabled-but-still-loaded; exact logical-name matching follows the never-flatten-namespaces rule, and matching never consults paths (a name selector is never a path selector).

design_decisions.decision: Finding severity is single-sourced from the §5.2 catalog in src/findings; normalizeFinding ignores caller-supplied severity. Finding status defaults to CONFIRMED, except SOURCE_NOT_ENUMERATED → UNKNOWN when the producer carries no status (the S0 canonicaliser's rule).
design_decisions.why: Three producers with three shapes must not be able to disagree about what a finding means.

design_decisions.decision: SYMLINK_OUTSIDE_ROOT discovery skips become P1 findings with status UNKNOWN (target never read → INCOMPLETE, never PASS). SYMLINK_LOOP, CANONICAL_PATH_UNRESOLVABLE, DEPTH_LIMIT, ENTRY_LIMIT and unreadable-entry skips become no finding: a loop contributes no skill content and the rest of the tree was still enumerated; a dangling link is not a skill.
design_decisions.why: Only unverifiable skill content can make an audit incomplete; traversal bounds are recorded in the discovery output, not in findings.

design_decisions.decision: An unreadable Codex config with no other unenumerated source is reported as unknown scope CONFIG (fail-closed). Inert on the S0 fixtures (c08 already lists PLUGIN/SYSTEM as unknown).
design_decisions.why: Mirrors the Codex PoC's own rule (unreadable config → INCOMPLETE) inside the kernel's uniform derivation, which keys INCOMPLETE off unknownScopes / UNKNOWN findings.

design_decisions.decision: npm script test:rules (vitest run tests/rules) added to package.json, following the T001/T005 precedent (test:identity, test:symlink, test:manifest were added the same way although the frozen §3.3 script list does not name them). No dependency or license-field change.
design_decisions.why: The task's acceptance command requires it; the §3.3 list is a contract for the gate scripts, and the per-area test scripts are the established extension point.

files_not_modified: S0 golden (tests/golden/s0/expected.json) — untouched; 48/48 cross-check reads it only.
T005 modules (src/identity, src/discovery, src/manifest) — untouched; the resolver only imports the SkippedEntry type from discovery.
PoC adapters (src/adapters/*) — untouched; the kernel consumes their results as values.
S0 gate scripts (scripts/s0-gate.mjs, s0-run.mjs, s0-canonical.mjs) — untouched.
03_evidence/S0/* — gate run rewrote only the base_commit label; restored from git before commit (gate hash unchanged).
forbidden_rules_verified: Unknown source never treated as an empty set (unknownScopes → INCOMPLETE; codex/c11, claude/c06, openmausbot/o13).
Name selector never used as a path selector (policy name matching consults logicalName only; comparePolicy takes no paths).
Claude plugin namespaces never flattened (forbidden 'deploy' does not match 'acme:deploy'; proven on claude/c03 and in policy unit tests).
OpenMausBot unread config never treated as default-off (o05/o15: FAIL_OPEN_CONFIG + unknown scope → INCOMPLETE; the kernel preserves the PoC finding and its unknown scope).
known_limitations: SYMLINK_ALIAS (§5.2, P2) is catalogued but not emitted by the T006 kernel: the PoCs already merge/dedupe aliases (Codex skill-scan merges them; Claude/OpenMausBot dedupe by canonical-path hash), so no unmerged alias is visible in PoC results. Emitting it needs a comparison of discovery output against PoC instances (T009 CLI work).

The kernel reports the current state only: a DISCOVERED instance in a forbidden scope produces no finding (it is not loadable), so a future flag flip that would load it is not warned about. That is a policy-monitoring concern, not an audit finding.

Policy findings come only from the policy argument passed to the kernel. A caller that runs the kernel without the profile policy gets no SCOPE_LEAK / DISABLE_MISMATCH findings (proven by test on claude/c07). T009 must load the profile policy and pass it through.

Kernel instance identity is the access-path key <sourceRootId>:<relativePath>, not the T005 physical-file identity (absolute canonical path). Two access paths to the same physical file are two kernel instances (correct for the audit: the host can address both); physical-file merging stays with IdentityRegistry.

The expected set is defined over ELIGIBLE instances only. A skill the policy expects enabled but which is DISABLED/DISCOVERED/INVALID/missing is not reported by any §5.2 finding id; the taxonomy has no 'expected-enabled but not loaded' finding, so the kernel does not invent one.
